sentences.text: Ram Adhar vs The State Of U.P. on 30 April, 2019

Author: Dinesh Kumar Singh
Bench: Dinesh Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
Court No. - 28
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 118 of 2004
Revisionist :- Ram Adhar

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- The State of U.P.
Counsel for Revisionist :- Saurabh Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt.Advocate
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1.

The present revision is directed against the judgement and order dated 11.3.2004 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge/Fast Track Court No.IV, Raebareli in Criminal Appeal No.10 of 2003,
which was preferred against the judgment and order dated 4.2.2003 passed by the Ist Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate/Judicial Magistrate of Economic Offences, Raebareli in Case No.1432 of 2002, whereby the revisionist was convicted and sentenced under Section 16(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (for short 'the Act') for six months simple imprisonment with a fine of Rs.1,000/- and for non-payment, one month additional sentence.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Fast Track Court No.IV, Raebareli
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Ist Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate/Judicial Magistrate of Economic Offences, Raebareli
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellate court had affirmed the judgement and order passed by the trial court and dismissed the appeal.

2. The facts of the case are that the Food Inspector Sri Upendra singh intercepted the revisionist,
who was taking 110 litres of milk in six cans on a Rickshaw for selling the same.
After introducing himself, he bought 750 ml milk for Rs.5.25/- and after preparing sample, sent it to public analyst for examination.
No one from the public came to be witness regarding sample etc.

The revisionist Ram Adhar vs The State Of U.P. on 30 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47403219/
1 refused to reveal the name of the owner of the milk.

entities.text: Ram Adhar vs The State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The public analyst in his report found the milk solids-not-fat much below of 18%, which is prescribed under the Act for the milk.
Since the milk sent for analysis was found to be adulterated one, a compliant was filed.
3. After examining the evidence and the submissions made, the trial court had convicted the revisionist.
On appeal, the appellate court also dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgement and order passed by the trial court.

4. Heard Sri Saurabh Srivastava, learned counsel representing the revisionist and Sri Ashwani Kumar Singh, learned AGA representing the State.
5.
Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the sample was taken on 29.7.1991 and analysis report was dated 3.9.1991.
The complaint was filed on 15.10.1992 and the notice was issued under Section 13(2) of the Act on 30.10.1992.

He, therefore, submits that the notice was not served within a period of six months and the samples become unfit for analysis after ten months and, therefore,
the sample along with the analysis report could not be sent to the Central Food Laboratory for further analysis.
He further submits that since there is violation of Section 13(2) of the Act, the whole proceedings got vitiated and the judgments and orders passed by the courts below are liable to be set aside.

6. In support of his submission, learned counsel for the revisionist has placed reliance upon the judgement of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in the case of Suresh Narayan and others v. State of M.P., 2003 FAJ 322.

entities.text: Suresh Narayan and others v. State of M.P., 2003 FAJ 322
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Paragraph six of the aforesaid judgement reads as under :-
"6.

Having heard the learned counsel for parties and having regard to the fact and legal position involved in the present case, this Court is of the opinion that allowing the proceedings/prosecution of the petitioners before the trial Court would be nothing but abuse of process of Court of law and the same would cause immense loss to the public exchequer and valuable time of the Court which are already heavily burdened with the cases.

In the present case, there is no dispute on the fact that the Food Inspector/respondent took sample on 5-4-1994 and the complaint was filed on 9-11-1995 as late as 19 months and for this delay, the prosecution cannot thrust blame on the petitioners.

This delay is required to be explained by the prosecution but even if they have genuine and reasonable explanation, the same will not help to them as it is the settled legal position that milk or milk products like ice cream etc.
gets deterioration within 10 month from the date of its lifting meaning thereby the sample may be fit for sending for further examination by the Central Food Laboratory within 10 months from the date of its purchase by the Food Inspector.
In the present case, complaint itself was filed after a lapse of 19 months.

Therefore, even if the sample would have been available the same could not be in a fit condition for further examination by Central Food Laboratory and accused has a right to apply under section 13(2) of the Act after institution of prosecution by the respondents and because of delay in institution of complaint, valuable right of the petitioners has been infringed.

Thus, there seems no justification to allow the continuation of the trial Ram Adhar vs The State Of U.P. on 30 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47403219/
2 against them.

entities.text: Ram Adhar vs The State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Supreme Court in both the above mentioned cases have considered this aspect and in the case of State of Haryana v. Unique Farmaid (supra) recorded its concurrence with the exercise of power under section 482 by the Punjab & Harayana High Court, quashing the proceedings pending against accused persons before the trial Court because the prosecution was filed after the lapse of long time and accused deprived of valuable right to get sample reanalised from Central Insecticide Laboratory which has prejudiced the case of the accused.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Unique Farmaid
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same is the factual and legal situation available in the present case.

Therefore, in the opinion of this Court,
the proceedings pending before the learned CJM, Indore in Case No. 5247/95 is liable to be quashed."

7. On the other hand, Sri Ashwani Kumar Singh, learned AGA submits that the revisionist gave wrong address and, therefore, notice could not be served and for his own wrong, he cannot be given the benefit.

Notice under Section 13(2) of the Act sent on time and because of the wrong address, it could not be served within time and, therefore, the submission of the learned counsel for the revisionist has no force and is liable to be rejected.
8.
I have considered the submissions of the rival parties carefully.
9. I do not find any infirmity or illegality in the impugned judgements and orders passed by the courts below.
However, considering the fact that the samples were taken in 1991 and the complaint was filed in 1992 and since then almost 27 years have gone.

10. Considering the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562, in which the Supreme Court after considering the age of the appellant in that case and taking into account the fact that the incident was very old, reduced the sentence to the period already undergone.
11.

entities.text: Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, it would be appropriate to dismiss the revision against conviction, but reduce the sentence to the period already undergone with a fine of Rs.5,000/- to be deposited by the revisionist within a period of one month.

12. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the revision is partly allowed while maintaining the conviction, but the sentence is reduced to the period already undergone with a fine of Rs.5,000/-.

(Dinesh Kumar Singh, J.) Order Date :- 30.4.2019 Rao/-
